subject: Forensic summary, timeline & remediation playbook for Oct 19 inference disruption
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lina Rodriguez <lina@alphafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interim empirical forensics & immediate mitigations (Oct 18 disruption)

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for flagging the degradation you saw yesterday. We wanted to share an initial, evidence-backed snapshot of what we’ve found so far and the short-term mitigation we’ve applied. We’ll follow with a full, validated playbook and verification artifacts within 48 hours.

Executive summary (short):
- Observed impact: intermittent request queuing and 10–15s token delays for a subset of long-sequence requests between 17:30–21:00 PDT on Oct 18.
- Root cause (initial forensic signal): a memory reclamation path in our batched CUDA kernel (custom path for multi-query fusion) was failing under sustained high-concurrency, causing device memory pressure and repeated attempt-to-reclaim cycles that delayed new batches.
- Immediate mitigation: we disabled the fused-batch kernel and reverted to the conservative batched path at 18:10 PDT; tail latency returned to expected ranges within ~6 minutes.

What we attached: a representative excerpt of device memory histograms and the short timeline CSV (forensics-log-sample.txt, timeline-csv.csv).

Short asks for you:
- Can you confirm whether AlphaFin saw production impact beyond the token delay window above (any errors, timeouts)?
- If AlphaFin can run its quick smoke test (3 requests of each long-sequence path) after 18:30 PDT, that will help us validate the revert.

Next steps from Redwood (what we’ll deliver):
1) Full validated timeline and causal chain with log hashes and relevant stack traces (delivery: Oct 21, EOD).
2) Hotfix patch to fused-batch kernel with test coverage (delivery: patch candidate and test matrix by Oct 22).
3) Preventative controls: autoscale guard for fused kernel, automated memory-pressure alarms, and a canary test for multi-query fusion (delivery: design doc Oct 25).

We’ll follow with a consolidated remediation playbook for your security/compliance team.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Attachment: forensics-log-sample.txt (excerpt), timeline-csv.csv
From: Lina Rodriguez <lina@alphafin.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@alphafin.com>, Marco Bianchi <m.bianchi@alphafin.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interim empirical forensics & immediate mitigations (Oct 18 disruption)

Sean —

Thanks for the quick update and the artifacts. Quick answers:
- We saw increased latency across our long-context enrichment route; no user-facing 5xx, but some upstream request timeouts triggered retries in our integration layer.
- We can run the smoke tests this afternoon and will share the results to the Drive link you provided.

Two asks from our side:
1) Please include specific log hashes and the exact builds involved so our SRE can map to our replay logs.
2) Procurement is asking for an ETA on the formal incident packet (timeline + mitigations + verification instructions) for our audit team.

Appreciate the revert. We’ll coordinate a verification call if needed.

Best,
Lina
Lina Rodriguez
Head of Platform Ops, AlphaFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: internal: quick tech notes and evidence to include

Folks —

Quick internal coordination notes to assemble the deliverable Sean will send to AlphaFin:
- Include these log hashes: hash:a9f4b2 (fusion kernel start), hash:c3d6e7 (OOM attempt), hash:1e0f4b (revert action). They map to prod builds: rwd-2026.10.17-3 and rwd-2026.10.17-4.
- Add a short explanation of the repro we ran: concurrent 32-client long-context replay with synthetic k=4 multi-query. Repro attached as part of the runbook.
- Capture metric snapshots: device free memory, kernel-queue depth, and scheduling-wait histogram at 10s granularity from 17:00–22:00.
- Suggested customer verification checklist (short): three smoke requests, compare token latency before/after revert, confirm no retry storms from upstream.

I’ll prep the mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf (includes test harness steps, expected traces and grep patterns) and hand it to Sean for external distribution.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lina Rodriguez <lina@alphafin.com>, Marco Bianchi <m.bianchi@alphafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated forensic packet + remediation playbook and verification instructions

Lina / Marco —

Attached is the consolidated packet we promised. Summary below and please see attachments for the evidence: mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf, timeline-csv.csv, forensics-log-sample.txt. We’ve also uploaded everything to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/forensics-summary (DOC-12345-ALPHAFIN).

Consolidated finding (concise):
- Causal chain: under sustained high concurrency the fused multi-query CUDA execution path enters a slow-path in our memory-reclaim flow due to a race condition between the kernel’s internal buffer pool and the device allocator. That race led to repeated reclamation attempts, increasing kernel latency and starving newer batches.
- Evidence: device memory histograms, stack traces from the failed reclaim, build hashes (rwd-2026.10.17-3 -> rwd-2026.10.17-4 where the regression was introduced), and the timeline CSV with event markers for 17:27, 18:10 (revert), and 18:16 (stability restored).

Immediate remediation already applied:
- Reverted to conservative kernel at 18:10 PDT (rolled back rwd-2026.10.17-3 to rwd-2026.10.17-2 path for fused execution).
- Temporary guard: raised autoscale threshold for the fused path and added an immediate alarm for sustained device reclaim activity > 30s.

Planned remedial actions and verification steps (playbook):
1) Hotfix and test: patch race in reclaim path + unit and integration tests (target: Oct 22).
2) Canary rollout: deploy patched build to 5% capacity with synthetic long-context traffic and automated alarm gating (target: Oct 24).
3) Control improvements: add canary for fused multi-query, memory-pressure dashboard panels, and deploy autoscale guard permanently (design complete Oct 25).
4) Customer verification run: AlphaFin to run the three-step smoke test (instructions in mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf) and provide test results in the Drive folder. We’ll schedule a joint verification window and log-hash comparison.

Requested timeline for AlphaFin: please confirm by Oct 22 whether you want us to schedule an on-call verification window Oct 23–25. If you prefer asynchronous verification, upload the smoke-run results to the Drive folder and we’ll validate and close.

Compensation & SLA note: we’ve logged this as a Sev-2 incident per our SLA definition. Our account team will follow up about credits/compensation options after verification completes.

If you want a single-page executive summary for your audit team, we can provide a signed incident packet with artifacts and timestamped log hashes.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf, timeline-csv.csv, forensics-log-sample.txt
